A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DeltaProduct, with matching authors, recurrence, and retained experiments. All 21 pages of v3 and 36 pages of v5, including appendices, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures supporting comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original DeltaProduct experiments on permutation groups, formal languages, language modeling, length extrapolation, and runtime.

after.justification: v5 retains original experimental results and adds scaling experiments, deeper state-tracking evaluations, throughput measurements, and hidden-state analyses.

M1.justification: The multiple gradient steps, Householder-product recurrence, gating, and interleaved implementation are retained. However, v5 specifies normalized SiLU(Wjx) keys where v3 specifies normalized Wjx. The PDFs do not establish whether this reflects an implementation change or correction of an abbreviated description.

E1.justification: The dedicated recall-intensive evaluation on SWDE, SQUAD, and FDA is removed: its columns in v3 Table 1 and task descriptions disappear from v5. The permutation groups, three formal-language tasks, FineWeb training, other lm-eval benchmarks, and four extrapolation corpora remain, including SlimPajama in the appendix.

E2.justification: The corresponding retained comparisons preserve their comparator sets, including Transformer++, Mamba, GLA, DeltaNet, and Gated DeltaNet in language modeling and the same formal-language baselines. RWKV-7 receives expanded theoretical comparison but is not added as an experimentally evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: v5 adds 4096-token training experiments at 213M, 392M, and 805M parameters with 19B, 35B, and 55B training tokens, using head-count and head-dimension controls; the old 2048-token experiments remain separately. It also extends S4/S5 depth evaluations to ten layers, introduces effective-rank diagnostics and smoothed per-token loss, and adds H100 throughput protocols.

E4.justification: v5 adds hidden-state effective-rank analyses across heads, layers, and sequence boundaries to investigate forgetting and extrapolation. It substantially expands parameter-matched scaling controls and depth sensitivity, and supplies plots for the restricted-eigenvalue failures previously summarized without figures. The existing reflection/PCA analysis and formal-language experiments remain.

E5.justification: v3 Appendix C specifies averaging runtime over 200 iterations after three burn-in iterations; v5 retains the latency curve without that reporting information. Both versions retain best-of-three-seeds reporting for formal-language results. No new confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures are documented.

E6.justification: v5 adds substantial scaling, throughput, and effective-rank results. New Table 3 reports average task accuracy of 48.55 for DeltaNet and 49.95 for DeltaProduct3 at 805M parameters/55B tokens. Expanded depth experiments report S4 fitting with six layers and S5 failing even with ten. Retained Table 2 and overlapping old language-model scores are unchanged; recall scores are removed. New settings do not establish same-setting gains over v3.

T1.justification: v5 adds spectral propositions, explicit architectural assumptions, general finite-group and regular-language constructions, orthogonal-group results, and an RWKV-7 instability counterexample. The old dihedral proof remains in Appendix B.4 with an additional one-layer case. Appendix B.5 also introduces an incorrect general equivalence: spectral radius at most one does not guarantee uniformly bounded matrix powers.

C1.justification: The theoretical contribution expands from the two-layer dihedral result to arbitrary finite-group word problems in three layers for nh>1 or four for nh=1, plus regular-language recognition at language-dependent finite depth. These become central abstract/introduction claims. The original empirical superiority and extrapolation claims largely remain.

C2.justification: v5 connects extrapolation failure to effective-rank growth and a resulting hidden-state distribution shift. It adds practical qualifications about large lookup tables, decoder bottlenecks, and stability versus expressivity, and acknowledges nonmonotonic benefits under head-count scaling. Conversely, its new blanket better-average-accuracy statement in Appendix C.2 is not supported by every unchanged Table 2 variant.

D1.justification: v5 supplies experiment-repository and direct implementation links, explicit SiLU/decoder details, model configurations in Table 6, H100 hardware information, and 10,500 total training GPU hours. These materially expand reproducibility documentation. Some earlier details disappear, including the latency experiment's precision, batch size, compilation settings, and averaging procedure.

R1.justification: v5 substantially develops positioning against Grazzi et al. and RWKV-7, comparing layer requirements, lookup-table costs, and stability guarantees. It adds relevant work on automata decomposition, effective rank, memory utilization, forgetting, and kernels. This goes beyond reference renumbering and publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: v5 extensively rewrites the theoretical narrative and experimental interpretation, separates Background from Related Work, introduces an implementation subsection, moves Chomsky experiments into the appendix, and reorganizes the appendices around spectral properties, expressivity, and experiments. The abstract and contribution list are substantially recast.

P2.justification: v5 adds an expressivity table, scaling/configuration tables, throughput bars, spectral diagrams, and extensive effective-rank panels. It redraws the cube illustration, revises extrapolation displays, relocates the old language-model table, and removes the redundant modular-arithmetic plot while retaining its table. Figure 12's S3 success statement conflicts with its plotted restricted-eigenvalue failures.

improvement.justification: v5 substantially addresses v3's explicitly unresolved small-nh, multilayer expressivity question through general constructions and stated assumptions. Broader parameter-matched scaling and direct hidden-state diagnostics also strengthen support for the method beyond additional parameter count. These gains outweigh the removed recall benchmarks and reduced timing documentation, although localized errors in the new stability discussion, Figure 12 caption, and formal-language interpretation reduce precision.
